Former Spain international midfielder Juan Mata has announced his retirement from professional football at the age of 38, bringing an end to a career that included a World Cup triumph and major honours with Chelsea and Manchester United. Mata, who earned 41 caps for Spain, was part of the country’s squad that won the 2010 FIFA World Cup in South Africa. He also played a key role in Spain’s success at the 2012 European Championship, scoring in their 4-0 victory over Italy in the final. The midfielder began his professional career after progressing through Real Madrid’s youth system before joining Valencia in 2007, where he established himself as one of Spain’s promising attacking players. His performances earned him a move to Chelsea in August 2011, where he won the UEFA Champions League, Europa League and FA Cup during his spell at Stamford Bridge. Following his departure from England, the Spaniard continued his career abroad, featuring for Turkish side Galatasaray and Japanese club Vissel Kobe. He later moved to Australia, where he represented Western Sydney Wanderers and Melbourne Victory. As reported by BBC Sport on Wednesday, announcing his retirement, Mata said that although he was stepping away from playing professionally, his connection with football would remain. “Football will never leave my life. “There are so many ways to continue loving the game, so many ways to keep using it as a vehicle for development. “I may stop playing professionally, but I will never stop being a footballer,” he said. Mata’s retirement brings to a close a career spanning several countries and some of European football’s biggest clubs. His achievements with Spain, Chelsea and Manchester United established him as one of the notable midfielders of his generation.
